answers.explanation: The writer says none of the many people around could tell him how to find Grant Hall or answer his questions.
The writer could not find out how to get to Grant Hall, which made the prospect less cheerful.
The darkness of ignorance is the writer's state before he found the notice board that gave him the information he needed.
The writer says the notice board was poorly placed and he was not sure how much of the responsibility was his.
The writer says he learnt an indelible lesson about reading notice boards to stay informed about the university.
The passage says there are many skills of communication, and listening is one of them.
The passage says good listening has nothing to do with the functioning of the auditory organs, so making sure the speaker is audible is not part of creative listening.
The passage says creative listening involves critical response and some argument, so an uncompromising rejection of the speaker's argument is not implied.
The passage analyses the process of listening and response in a reasoned, explanatory way.
The passage is about listening as a skill within communication, so Listening in Communication is the most suitable title.
The passage describes the problems students face when working in English as a foreign language, as the medium of instruction.
The passage says difficulties arise when English is used as a medium of instruction.
The phrase means his English lets him down and he comes across as dull, cold or rude.
The statement implies the language can make the student behave badly, as the passage says of his dullness, coldness or rudeness.
The passage says unknown items of grammar and vocabulary appear in the texts, which are the most likely source of difficulty.
Manic pleasure is an excessive, almost frenzied pleasure, closest to unlimited pleasure.
Must kick it means the child is obliged to kick it and make it collapse.
The passage says the builder must destroy the tower himself, which gives him the pleasure.
The passage explains the destructive stage as growing out of the child's recent experience of sudden falls.
The passage says that the child feels stronger knowing there is somebody weaker, which is a feeling of strength.
The passage says she walks to town with eggs as an excuse to spend the day at the market, so she comes purposely to enjoy herself.
A dying art is one that is disappearing, so the goldsmith's trade is no longer popular.
The passage describes an African market scene, which is its main content.
The passage presents the market as a place people come to for business or for pleasure.
The passage mentions sandals, gold trinkets and eggs as items sold in the market.
